chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn 'Isa ibn 'Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to us. He said: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon them) wrote to one of his Shi'a followers in Baghdad:
In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

May God protect us and you from sedition — for if He does, then what a great blessing it would be! And if He does not, then that is perdition. We hold that argumentation regarding the Quran is an innovation (bid'a) in which the questioner and the answerer are equally partners: the questioner ventures into what is not his right, and the answerer takes upon himself what is not incumbent upon him. There is no creator but God, and everything other than Him is created. The Quran is the speech of God — do not assign it a name from yourself, lest you be among the misguided.
May God make us and you of those who fear their Lord in the unseen, and who are in awe of the Hour.

key_terms.الجدال: Argumentation, disputation — theological debate condemned as bid'a here
key_terms.الضالين: The misguided — those who give unauthorized names to the Quran
key_terms.الغيب: The unseen — what is beyond human perception, feared only through faith
key_terms.الفتنة: Sedition/tribulation — here referring to the theological controversy over the createdness of the Quran
key_terms.كلام الله: The speech of God — the Imam's preferred term for the Quran, avoiding either 'created' or 'uncreated'

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Hadi say about debating the createdness of the Quran?
ai.summary: This is a letter from Imam 'Ali al-Hadi (the tenth Imam, peace be upon him) written to one of his followers in Baghdad, addressing the bitter controversy of his era over whether the Quran was 'created' (makhluq) or 'uncreated' — a debate that had raged under the Abbasid caliphs and led to the persecution of scholars. The Imam takes a decisive stance: the Quran is the speech of God, and one must not apply labels to it from one's own reasoning. Both those who ask about the issue and those who answer are equally culpable, since it is an innovation to engage in such disputation. The letter closes with a prayer echoing Quran 21:49, affirming that the goal of the believer is reverent awe of the unseen Lord.
